title: Processes and signals
summary: ps, top, kill and the signals behind it, jobs, & and nohup.

steps.title: Every program is a process
body: A running program is a **process** with a **PID**, a parent (PPID), an owner and state.
USER   PID %CPU %MEM    VSZ   RSS TTY  STAT START TIME COMMAND
$ pgrep -a dotnet      # PIDs + command lines matching a name
$ top                  # live view; P sorts by CPU, M by memory, q quits
`htop` is a friendlier `top` (install it). PID 1 (`systemd` on most distros) is the ancestor of everything.

steps.prompt: The server is slow. Which command shows you, **live**, which process is eating the CPU?
steps.explain: `ps` is a snapshot; `top`/`htop` refresh continuously. `df -h` is disk space.

steps.title: Signals
body: `kill` doesn't necessarily kill: it **sends a signal**.
| `SIGTERM` | 15 | "please exit" (the default). Programs can clean up. |
| `SIGKILL` | 9 | the kernel ends it now. Can't be caught: no cleanup, no flushing. |
| `SIGHUP` | 1 | terminal closed; many daemons treat it as "reload config" |
Etiquette: TERM, wait a few seconds, only then KILL.

steps.prompt: Arrange the polite way to stop a stuck process 912.
steps.explain: Ask first (TERM), give it time, check whether it's still there, and only force it if it is.

steps.prompt: Match the signal to when it's sent.

steps.title: Jobs: &, fg, bg, nohup
body: $ ./long-task.sh &        # start in the background, get the prompt back
$ fg %1                   # bring job 1 to the foreground
$ bg %1                   # let it continue in the background
Background jobs still belong to your terminal: **close the SSH session and they get SIGHUP** and usually die.
nohup ./long-task.sh > task.log 2>&1 &     # ignore SIGHUP, log to a file
For anything long-lived use `tmux`/`screen` for interactive work, or a proper **systemd service** (next lesson).

steps.prompt: You started a 2-hour migration with `./migrate.sh &` over SSH, then your Wi-Fi dropped. When you reconnect, it's gone. What would have prevented this?
steps.explain: The dropped session sent SIGHUP to its jobs. nohup ignores it; tmux keeps a session alive on the server you can reattach to.
Job 1 was terminated (bash may report it once), so only job 2 remains. `+` marks the current job.

steps.title: pgrep
steps.prompt: Write `List<int> Pgrep(List<string> ps, string name)` over `ps -eo pid,ppid,user,cmd` output: the first line is the header; every other line has PID, PPID, USER and then the command (which may contain spaces), separated by one or more spaces and possibly leading spaces. Return the PIDs whose **command** contains `name`, in order.
hints: `Split(' ', 4, StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries)` keeps the command in one piece.
template: var dojoPs = new List<string> { "  PID  PPID USER CMD", "    1     0 root /sbin/init", "  912     1 www  dotnet /srv/api/Api.dll --urls http://*:5000", "  913   912 www  dotnet /srv/api/worker.dll", " 1200  1100 ana  grep dotnet" };
Dojo.Eq("user column is not the command", new List<int>(), Pgrep(dojoPs, "www"));
